authority_treatment.reason: The Court expressly maintains possession protection despite failure to prove plaintiff title for the same suit land; possession still requires its own judicial finding.

The Court adopts protection for settled possession while distinguishing incipient trespass, permitted resistance, peaceful recapture and judicial recovery. It supplies no mechanically executable test or case-specific factor-by-factor chronology; earlier precedent is reported, not independently verified.
The Court approves protecting established settled possession from defendant obstruction by injunction; this is an independent possessory ground, not proven use of force or an award of title.

The merits-stage court rejects automatic dismissal for title non-proof or the asserted absence of declaration where possession supplies a basis; it distinguishes a temporary-injunction decision and does not decide all procedural contexts.
The Court adopts the distinction between possessory and proprietary remedies and expressly avoids adjudicating either party’s title. Salmond and precedent appear only through the target judgment.

The Court expressly allows properly constituted future title proceedings; any defendant eviction depends on first proving a better possessory right. It makes no future merits or procedural determination.

decisive_counterarguments: The appellant contended that omitting a declaration of title rendered the suit defective; the Supreme Court rejected automatic dismissal in this merits-stage case (IK-789051:L68-L69; L109-L112).

The appellant separately argued that plaintiff title non-proof required dismissal irrespective of established possession or defendant title; the Court found no merit in this submission (IK-789051:L69).

Sri Dasnam Naga Sanyasi was invoked against an injunction-only suit, but the Supreme Court described it as a discretionary temporary-injunction decision on its own facts, not a merits-stage automatic bar (IK-789051:L108-L110).

Settled possession is necessary: stray, intermittent, incipient or incomplete trespass can be resisted with no more force than permitted; the duration, knowledge, acquiescence and possessory-intention factors are not independently proved here (IK-789051:L88-L105).

Even a rightful owner may need judicial process against settled possession, while a wrongfully dispossessed rightful owner may retake land peacefully and a claimant proving better right may seek judicial eviction; the protective rule is not immunity from lawful recovery (IK-789051:L85-L87; L107).

Neither side proved title sufficient for its proposed consequence, and the apparent boundary dispute remains unresolved; possession-based injunction and dismissed appeal do not settle either ownership or demarcation (IK-789051:L65-L67; L106-L107; L113-L114).
coverage_limits: Only the supplied complete judgment and user-supplied rule registry, premises, candidates and mappings were used; no outside legal sources or other cases were inspected.
All factual and lower-court propositions are attributed to the Supreme Court’s text; underlying pleadings, exhibits, witness evidence and earlier decisions were not independently authenticated.
OPEN_TEXT recorded conclusions reflect only the expressly reported settled-possession classification for E1/E3; they are not independently executed legal tests.
FALSE for F14 is limited to the classification implied by an express positive finding, not independent historical proof of no intermittent trespass.
Competing claims, ownership and land-boundary identification remain unresolved. The defendant’s assertion and interference are one reported episode; actual physical force is not established.
The appellant’s contrary arguments are attributed PARTY_CLAIM propositions and are useful as opposition without being treated as true legal rules.
The final appellate dismissal is not an input proving its own premises. Subsequent title litigation and eviction are conditional and prospective, not outcomes already obtained.
Case-specific translations and the target court’s characterizations of cited precedents are not universal rules or independent precedent verification.
This is model research review, not human gold, legal approval, judicial endorsement, or a prediction.
